name: Improper Initialization
principle: The product fails to initialize a resource or initializes it to the wrong value before use. This leaves variables, memory, objects, locks, configuration, or security state in an unexpected state that can leak data, bypass checks, or crash.
detection_signals: C/C++ local variable declared without initializer and later read: `int x; ... use(x);`
C/C++ struct allocated by `malloc` and partially assigned before field reads or serialization
security flag or auth variable assigned only inside `if`/`switch` branch and used after the branch
`initialized` or `isReady` guard declared as `true` before initialization routine runs
buffer reused and sent via `send`, `write`, `fwrite`, or response API without `memset`, `calloc`, or full overwrite
object fields read before constructor/init method assigns all required fields
initialization failure path logs error but continues to use the resource
negative_signals: variable initialized at declaration or immediately before first use
all `if`/`else` and `switch default` paths assign the variable before later use
C/C++ allocation uses `calloc`, value-initialization `{}`, or constructor that initializes all fields
security-sensitive default is deny/false/invalid, e.g. `authenticated=false` or `uid=-1`
initialization API return value is checked and failure path returns, throws, or aborts before use
shared initialization is protected by `mutex`, `synchronized`, or `std::call_once`
false_defense_traps: using a boolean `initialized` flag but setting it before initialization completes
checking only the success path while exception/error paths leave fields unset
relying on comments or naming conventions instead of constructor/default initialization
clearing only part of a struct while padding or unused fields are still serialized
verification_focus: Can any execution path access the resource before it is explicitly and correctly initialized to a safe value?

consequence_chains.trigger: resource is accessed before initialization completes
consequence_chains.consequence: unpredictable value, crash, or unintended control flow

consequence_chains.trigger: uninitialized variable controls index, pointer, privilege, or branch
consequence_chains.consequence: out-of-bounds access, access-control bypass, or denial of service

consequence_chains.trigger: security-sensitive state defaults to allow, admin, root, or enabled
another thread observes a partially initialized resource
consequence_chains.consequence: use of inconsistent state or protection bypass

patch_principle: Initialize every variable, field, buffer, and resource before first use.
Use safe defaults for security state: deny, false, invalid, or least privilege.
Cover all branches, error paths, exceptions, and early returns with initialization or fail-stop behavior.
Use constructors, `calloc`, value-initialization, `memset`, or reset methods to fully initialize reused storage.
Synchronize one-time initialization and publish the resource only after initialization succeeds.
